correctness.rationale: Under nλ_n^r→c and λ_n→0, the exact Poisson variance gives λhat/λ→1; binomial Chebyshev handles cells below r; N_{n,r}⇒Pois(c/r!) by an explicit pgf; n Pr(X≥r+1)→0 eliminates every upper cell. The exact infinite weighted tail plus Slutsky proves all finite and supremum limits; small data-adaptive masses and the same decomposition prove their collapse. Plateau limits use nq_{n,r}→∞ instead. The standalone checker passed 367 supplementary checks but is not a substitute for this proof.

value.rationale: For the published family of nine Poisson goodness-of-fit distances, a true sparse null produces a nonzero, atomic limiting score under fixed exponential weights while both data-adaptive weighting families vanish. Every rare count cell creates a distinct exact null phase, quantitatively locating a calibration boundary not addressed by fixed-mean power simulations. The result is about diagnostic behavior, not an unsupported assertion of false test size.
